_comment: Recurring checks that are not tied to a commit, and so have no natural trigger.
Read by scripts/jobs.py; surfaced at session start (docs/reference/SESSION_START.md).
`next_due` is the earliest `last_run + interval_days` across all jobs, so a session
can decide whether anything needs doing by reading one field instead of reasoning
about every entry. scripts/jobs.py rewrites it; do not maintain it by hand.
`last_run` is state in a tracked file, which is a deliberate trade: the schedule
travels with the repo and is visible to everyone, at the cost of a one-line diff
per run. On a merge conflict, keep the LATER timestamp - it is the one that
A job with no `command` is a human checklist item: jobs.py reports it as due and
records when it was marked done, but runs nothing.

jobs.description: Is a newer openspec release out than the one that generated our skills?
jobs.notes: Also checked by .github/workflows/openspec-version-check.yml, which files an issue. This entry is the local half: it catches the update while someone is actually here to apply it.

jobs.description: cargo audit and npm audit; findings go to docs/BACKLOG.md with severity
jobs.notes: SESSION_START.md §4. No command: cargo audit needs the toolchain and npm audit needs both UIs, and a half-run audit reporting 'ok' would be worse than no audit.

jobs.description: Do the VEN's hexagonal dependency rules still hold, and does the module diagram still describe the code?
jobs.notes: The four dependency rules are now scripted (scripts/audit_ven_architecture.py) and run automatically. The module diagram in docs/architecture/module_dependency_graph.md is hand-maintained and is the part that still needs a human pass: compare its nodes against VEN/src/tasks/, the controller ports, and anything new under infra. Its first check (2026-09-23) found it six task loops and the whole fleet-telemetry path behind.

jobs.description: Compare DOCUMENTATION.md and docs/architecture/ against the actual code
